assumptions: The supplied .tar is binary and unreadable by the permitted read-only file reader; the unpacked copy at bundles/seven-p1-r3/ was treated as the artifact content per the scope instruction to review the unpacked bundle file by file. The tar's SHA-256 could not be independently recomputed without a hashing tool.

Per-file SHA-256 values (tasks/architecture/task-dag/execution-contract) were not recomputed; they were verified for internal cross-consistency across drift-lock.json, execution-prompt.md, and replan-record.json after_hashes.

External files referenced by the bundle (replan-history/previous, infrastructure-tasks.json, infrastructure-plan.md, rework-plan-check-sh.log, handoff-validation.json, task-identity-map.json) are assumed to exist in the repository change directory with the digests recorded in replan-record.json.

Count verification used the file contents directly: 39 DAG nodes/waves, 92 V_* scenario checks + 16 supplemental/infra checks + 10 rework checks = 118, matching handoff and replan-record identity_preserved.

findings.claim: r2 codex finding #1 is fixed in-artifact: journey execution order semantics now require the real-Comet recovery fault window to be injected within the same product Run before its completed step, and no post-completed re-enactment is permitted.
findings.evidence: execution-contract.json journey_execution.order_semantics (line 3841) and same_run_rule (line 3838); V_SAME_RUN_DELIVERY expected text (line 3663) references the same-Run window via order_semantics; V_RW_REAL_COMET_RECOVERY expected (line 3597) states the kill occurs during V_SAME_RUN_DELIVERY's product Run before completed.

findings.claim: r2 codex finding #2 is fixed in-artifact: replan-record after_hashes were refreshed and the refreshed digests are consistent across drift-lock.json and execution-prompt.md.
findings.evidence: replan-record.json after_hashes (lines 31-38, incl. consensus_fix_20261022 note) match drift-lock.json plan/architecture/dag/execution_contract sha256 fields (lines 5-8) and execution-prompt.md locked hashes (lines 36-39); drift-lock amendment env-capability-20261022 (lines 474-484) records the same consensus-fix scope.

findings.claim: The env-capability-20261022 amendment records the superseded plan/architecture digests only as 8-hex prefixes, weakening byte-exact provenance of the superseded generation compared to the 64-hex digests used everywhere else.
findings.evidence: drift-lock.json lines 479-482: supersedes_hashes {"plan":"eb7ed2cb","architecture":"66ac6e36"} vs full 64-char digests in replan-record.json before_hashes and drift-lock top-level fields.
findings.recommendation: Record full 64-hex digests for superseded plan/architecture states in the next bundle revision.

findings.claim: Some retained pre-existing check commands embed flags that plain `node --test` may reject (e.g. `--scenario method-state-scope --json` appended to `node --test` invocations), risking command-level failures that must not be misread as behavior RED/FAIL.
findings.evidence: execution-contract.json V_P1_6_PONYTAIL_ASSETS command (line 3328) and V_I02_METHOD_STATE_SCOPE command (line 3386) use `node --test ... --scenario ... --json`; by contrast the 10 rework checks use valid `--test-reporter=tap`/`--test-name-pattern` forms (e.g. lines 3415, 3474). HANDOFF.md line 53 explicitly mandates re-verifying the actual commands/environments of the existing 108 checks.
findings.recommendation: During P3_1/owner re-verification, normalize these commands to valid node --test flag forms or wrapper CLIs before relying on their exit codes.

findings.claim: The bundle is not fully self-contained: it cites evidence files not packaged (rework-plan-check-sh.log, handoff-validation.json, infrastructure-tasks.json, replan-history/previous) and discloses that `bash scripts/check.sh` could not run to completion on the planning host due to a read-only os.utime fixture, so plan-level validation is partial and honestly not claimed as a pass.
findings.evidence: HANDOFF.md line 95 (check.sh limitation, no waiver of V_FULL_CHECK); execution-contract.json V_INFRA_I0x checks defer oracles to infrastructure-tasks.json (e.g. lines 3066, 3105); replan-record.json history pointer (line 6).
findings.recommendation: Ship the referenced logs and infrastructure task oracles (or their digests) inside the handoff bundle so receivers can validate frozen inputs without repo access.

summary: Reviewed the unpacked r3 bundle file by file (HANDOFF.md, tasks.md, architecture.md, task-dag.json, execution-contract.json, drift-lock.json, spec-baseline.json, execution-prompt.md, replan-record.json). Scope conformance verified: 39 DAG nodes with 39 serial single-node waves in a topologically valid fixed order; 118 required checks = 92 scenario checks + 16 supplemental/infra checks + 10 rework checks, matching handoff counts and acceptance_aggregation; three full journeys owned by VERIFY with construction-task scopes separated from full-journey acceptance; amendment 3 (SDD_HOME projectization with llmwiki pin 075c5b4/venv llmwiki-311 and Docker via user-visible terminal channel with receipts, sandbox EPERM honestly recorded) present in architecture.md, execution-prompt.md item 0, and tasks.md P1_1. Both r2 codex REJECT items are verifiably fixed: journey_execution.order_semantics plus V_SAME_RUN_DELIVERY/V_RW_REAL_COMET_RECOVERY same-Run-before-completed wording, and replan-record after_hashes refresh consistent with drift-lock and execution-prompt digests. Boundaries are tight: sole planner/product controllers, observer cannot write phase, helper finalize forbidden, and exactly three limited-artifact edges (P2_5←P2_4, I02←P2_4, I02←P2_5) enumerated identically in task-dag dependency_readiness and execution-contract with INTEGRATED_AWAITING_REAL_QUALIFICATION status rule and no waiver at VERIFY. Security posture keeps secrets out of Git, requires real role isolation and permission negatives, and routes Docker through the visible terminal channel. Remaining weaknesses are minor and non-blocking: truncated superseded-digest prefixes in the env-capability amendment, questionable flag syntax in a few retained legacy check commands (covered by the mandated recheck of the 108 existing checks), and a not-fully-self-contained bundle with an honestly disclosed partial scripts/check.sh run. No blocking findings; I would authorize the gated next step now.
